No unsold or asking entries survive. No Australian or Tasmanian 18ct hunter result was found (Gowans has none; WebSearch cap reached so Armitage past results could not be searched). The A$230 Gowans 9ct ladies' watch is a floor only and sits outside the range.
lots.working: No max bid. The SOLD results are UK, different makers and types (one full hunter with chain at 116g of 18ct gold, one small 40g Swiss half hunter), and lot 874's carat, hallmark and weight are all unseen in the photos. Value is mostly gold weight, so a hammer limit cannot be set honestly until weight and the 18 hallmark are confirmed. For scale only: if confirmed 18ct and gents size, the Capt (40g, A$2,104) and Omega (A$3,061) half hunters suggest something like A$2,000 to 3,000 hammer at UK auction; a keep limit on that basis would be 2,104/1.22 = A$1,724, round down A$1,720, but this is NOT applied because the item is not shown to be the same.
lots.confidence_reason: Hallmark and weight not read; dial maker name illegible; comparables are UK and not like-for-like; no Australian SOLD result.

lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD = A$600 (Gowans 15ct 5.1g pair); 600 / 1.22 = 491.80, round down to A$490. Flip: likely resale A$600 hammer in a Tasmanian room; less assumed 15% vendor commission (A$90) and A$0 postage (local auction) = A$510; 510 / 2.44 = 209.0, round down to A$205. Both limits assume lot 905 weighs about 5g; if it weighs less, scale down (the Gowans pair implies about A$118 per gram hammer for 15ct, so 4g would be about A$470 resale, keep limit about A$385). lots.working: No max bid: the only same-pattern SOLD results are older than 24 months (latest Amelia 2024-07-27) and are large services, not a 19-piece part lot. For scale only: 19 pieces x US$16 to 35 = US$304 to 665 = A$440 to 960 at US auction. Local scrap-plus floor: 7 solid forks at perhaps 45 to 55g each (weight unknown) x A$2.1/g is about A$660 to 800 hammer, plus the knives at about A$20 each, but fork weight must be confirmed before relying on that.
lots.confidence_reason: Mark read clearly, but no SOLD support within 24 months, no Australian Kirk result, fork weight unknown, and the guide rests on old US sales and dealer asks.
